correctness.rationale: For pointwise Jordan BV the two monotone parts from the variation function have increments summing to Var(f). Their level sets are half-lines with either convention, so the layer integral controls the error including exceptional grid and endpoint values; each nonconstant indicator has variation one. The binomial tail is the specified beta CDF, and split integration gives the mean absolute deviation at a step. Convexity and reflection give the finite maximum; truncated first moments give the rational formula. Independently checked 528 grid cases through degree 32 and their reflections with exact Bernstein antiderivatives (`/workspace/reproductions/bernstein.py`). The beta CLT on every interior subsequence and uniform integrability from the rescaled second moments give sqrt(2p(1-p)/pi); the same moment bounds give zero at p=0,1. The midpoint lower bound forces all maximizing grid indices to approach the midpoint. Convexity extends this to any asymptotically norming jumps by moving to an endpoint of the containing cell with no loss. In particular the proof handles n=1 and permits incompatible-with-trace pointwise values that are charged to the Jordan variation.

evidence: The Stancu theorem gives the full b-dependent transition; its subcritical branch includes b=0 with limit 1/sqrt(2pi) and midpoint localization. It uses canonical right-continuous representatives and matching endpoint traces. The Kantorovich, King-modified and Durrmeyer records instead change the operator.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Scope differences in the latter operators do not establish coverage. The Stancu theorem is broader in operator parameter, not in data representatives; the exact overlap and routine representative extension are the decisive comparison.
